newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria cenbank sees 1997 budget on course.
newsitem.headline: Austria cenbank sees 1997 budget on course.

text.p: Austria's central bank said on Monday the government budget deficit in the first half of the year stood at 2.9 percent of GDP, putting Austria on course to meet the criteria for Europe's planned single currency.
National Bank director Adolf Wala told reporters revenues in the first six months had risen by 18 billion schillings while expenditure had fallen by six billion.
"The budget's development so far gives grounds for optimism," he said.
Wala was echoing comments last week by Chancellor Viktor Klima. He said the government aimed to stabilise the budget deficit below the Maastricht treaty's three percent threshold.
According to government estimates, this year's budget deficit should come in at between 2.6 and 2.7 percent of GDP.
The Organisation for Economic and Cooperation has forecast Austria's deficit will hit 3.0 percent this year and rise to 3.4 percent in 1998. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
